### Global Metadata
A complete 90-second traditional Japanese bon-odori dance piece for a circle of townspeople dancing around a lantern-lit yagura tower, steady and repetitive so dancers can follow it. 96 BPM, A minor pentatonic. A steady two-beat taiko ondo rhythm, shamisen riffs, a shinobue flute melody, chappa hand cymbals, soft koto in the background. Pure instrumental ensemble piece.

### Vocal Details
None. Instrumental only: the flute plays the dance melody; the shamisen answers every phrase; the taiko never stops.

### Timed Arrangement
0-10 seconds: a single taiko sets the ondo two-beat rhythm. 10-40 seconds: shamisen riff and flute melody in call and response. 40-70 seconds: the same dance tune repeats with chappa cymbals and koto added. 70-90 seconds: the full dance tune once more, steady. Keep tempo, texture and loudness consistent from start to end; no big climax. The piece must play for the full 90 seconds and must not end early, ending cleanly on the tonic so it can loop.
